message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limits: 35 mph (residential), 55 mph (interstate), 70 mph (interstate), 75 mph (interstate).
• Rural roads: 55 mph (interstate), 70 mph (interstate), 75 mph (interstate).
• Posted limits apply; exceeding by 5 mph or more can trigger a ticket. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a $50 fine. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education classes, and possible jail time. | | **Traffic Signal & Stop‑Sign Rules** | • Red lights: stop before the line or intersection.
• Yellow lights: stop if safe; otherwise proceed.
• Stop signs: come to a complete stop before proceeding. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens.
• Yield to traffic on the main road when turning onto a secondary road. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 20 mph during school hours; 25 mph during other times.
• Violations can lead to a $100 fine. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the driver is moving left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking on the curb is prohibited in many areas. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (2 / 32 inches).
• Mirrors must be properly adjusted. | | **Insurance & Registration** | • Minimum liability insurance required.
• Vehicle registration must be renewed annually.
• Failure to register can result in a $200 fine. | | **Accident Reporting** | • Must report accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 to the police within 24 hours.
• Failure to report can lead to a $500 fine. | ### Quick Tips - **Always obey posted signs** – they’re the law. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on your phone. - **Check your insurance** – it’s not just a formality. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – faulty brakes or lights can be ticketable. For detailed statutes, consult the Texas Transportation Code or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles website.
